cards.ja: 一部の都市では、自転車のシェアサービスが人気になっています。ある場所で自転車を借りて、別の場所で返すことができます。これは短い距離を移動したい人にとって便利です。自転車専用レーンを作った都市もあります。そうすることで、自転車に乗るのをより安全にしています。その結果、これらの都市では車を使う人が減っています。

steps.q: According to the passage, how are some cities making it safer for people to ride bicycles?
steps.ja: 文章によると、一部の都市はどのようにして自転車に乗るのをより安全にしていますか。
steps.model: By building special lanes for bicycles.
steps.hint: By ...ing の形で、「そうすることで(By doing so)」の前の文を使おう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Ms. Tanaka was visiting a city."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Ms. Tanaka was visiting a city.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：田中さんが旅行先の町の駅前で地図を見て、美術館まで遠いことに気づいている。／2コマめ：田中さんがスマートフォンを使ってシェアサイクルを借りている。／3コマめ：田中さんが自転車専用レーンを走って、美術館に着いている。
steps.model: One day, Ms. Tanaka was visiting a city. She wanted to go to a museum, but when she looked at the map, she found that it was far from the station. Then she noticed a bike-sharing service and rented a bicycle with her smartphone. She rode it on a bicycle lane and arrived at the museum quickly.
steps.hint: 「One day, Ms. Tanaka was visiting a city.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that people should ride bicycles instead of driving cars. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「人々は車を運転する代わりに自転車に乗るべきだ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. Riding a bicycle is good for our health. Also, bicycles do not produce any gas, so they are better for the environment than cars.
steps.hint: I agree. / I disagree. と立場を言ってから、because で理由を続けよう。

steps.q: Do you think Japanese cities should have more bicycle lanes?
steps.ja: 日本の都市はもっと自転車専用レーンを作るべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. In many cities, people ride bicycles on narrow sidewalks, so it is dangerous for people who are walking. If there are more bicycle lanes, there will be fewer accidents.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. と答えてから、理由を2つ言おう。

cards.title: Visitors from Abroad
cards.passage: The number of foreign tourists visiting Japan has been growing. Some of them have trouble finding their way because they cannot read Japanese. Many train stations now have signs written in several languages. In this way, foreign tourists can travel around more easily. Some stations also have staff members who can speak English or Chinese.
cards.ja: 日本を訪れる外国人観光客の数は増え続けています。日本語が読めないので、道がわからなくなって困る人もいます。今では多くの駅に複数の言語で書かれた案内板があります。このようにして、外国人観光客はより簡単に移動できます。英語や中国語を話せる職員がいる駅もあります。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can foreign tourists travel around more easily?
steps.ja: 文章によると、外国人観光客はどのようにしてより簡単に移動できますか。
steps.model: Because many train stations have signs written in several languages.
steps.hint: In this way の前の文を見て、Because many train stations ... と答えよう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Haruto was waiting for a train at the station."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Haruto was waiting for a train at the station.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：駅のホームでハルトが電車を待っていると、外国人の観光客が地図を持って困っている。／2コマめ：ハルトが英語で話しかけて、乗る電車を教えている。／3コマめ：二人が同じ電車に乗り、観光客がハルトにお礼のポストカードを渡している。
steps.model: One day, Haruto was waiting for a train at the station. He saw a tourist from another country who was holding a map and looked confused. Haruto spoke to him in English and told him which train to take. They got on the same train together. The tourist thanked Haruto and gave him a postcard from his country.
steps.hint: 「One day, Haruto was waiting for a train at the station.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that everyone in Japan should learn English. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「日本ではみんなが英語を学ぶべきだ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. English is used in many countries, so it is useful for traveling and working. Also, we can help foreign tourists who visit Japan.
steps.hint: まず I agree. か I disagree. を言い、理由を2つ（Also, ...）挙げよう。

steps.q: Do you think the number of foreign tourists in Japan will keep increasing?
steps.ja: 日本を訪れる外国人観光客の数は増え続けると思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Many people around the world are interested in Japanese food and culture. Also, Japan is a safe country, so tourists can enjoy traveling here.
steps.hint: Yes. か No. のあと、For example, ... で具体例を入れよう。

cards.title: Walking for Health
cards.passage: Walking is one of the easiest ways to stay healthy. Some towns hold walking events in which people walk together along rivers or through forests. Participants can enjoy beautiful scenery while getting exercise. Some events also give prizes to people who walk a certain number of steps. By doing so, the towns hope to encourage more people to walk regularly.
cards.ja: 歩くことは健康を保ついちばん簡単な方法の一つです。人々が一緒に川沿いや森の中を歩くウォーキングイベントを開く町もあります。参加者は運動しながら美しい景色を楽しむことができます。一定の歩数を歩いた人に賞品をあげるイベントもあります。そうすることで、町はより多くの人が定期的に歩くようになることを願っています。

steps.q: According to the passage, how do the towns hope to encourage more people to walk regularly?
steps.ja: 文章によると、町はどのようにして、より多くの人が定期的に歩くようにしたいと考えていますか。
steps.model: By giving prizes to people who walk a certain number of steps.
steps.hint: By ...ing の形で、「そうすることで(By doing so)」の前の文を使おう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Mr. Suzuki's doctor told him to exercise more."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Mr. Suzuki's doctor told him to exercise more.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：病院で、医者が鈴木さんに「もっと運動しましょう」と言っている。／2コマめ：鈴木さんが家族と一緒に川沿いのウォーキングイベントに参加している。／3コマめ：イベントのゴールで、鈴木さんが賞品をもらって笑っている。
steps.model: One day, Mr. Suzuki's doctor told him to exercise more. When he got home, he found out about a walking event in his town. On the weekend, he joined the event with his family, and they walked along the river. At the finish line, Mr. Suzuki received a prize because he had walked many steps. He decided to walk every day.
steps.hint: 「One day, Mr. Suzuki's doctor told him to exercise more.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that people today do not get enough exercise. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「今の人々は十分な運動をしていない」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. Many people sit at their desks all day at work or school. Also, they use cars or elevators instead of walking, so they do not move their bodies much.
steps.hint: I think ... / I don't think ... で始めて、because のあとに理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think companies should give workers time to exercise?
steps.ja: 会社は社員に運動する時間を与えるべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. If workers exercise, they will stay healthy and take fewer days off. Also, exercising helps them reduce stress, so they can work better.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. を言ってから、because ... と Also, ... で理由をつなげよう。

cards.title: Recycling Clothes
cards.passage: Many people throw away clothes they no longer wear. However, some clothing stores have started to collect old clothes from customers. The stores give the clothes to people in need or turn them into new materials. In this way, they can reduce the amount of waste. Customers who bring old clothes sometimes receive discount coupons.
cards.ja: 多くの人がもう着なくなった服を捨てています。しかし、お客さんから古着を回収し始めた衣料品店もあります。お店はその服を困っている人にあげたり、新しい素材に作り変えたりします。このようにして、ごみの量を減らすことができます。古着を持ってきたお客さんは割引券をもらえることもあります。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can some clothing stores reduce the amount of waste?
steps.ja: 文章によると、一部の衣料品店はどのようにしてごみの量を減らすことができますか。
steps.model: By giving old clothes to people in need or turning them into new materials.
steps.hint: 「このようにして(In this way)」の前の文を見て、By ...ing で答えよう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Aya was cleaning her room."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Aya was cleaning her room.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：アヤが部屋を片付けていて、小さくなった服がたくさんある。／2コマめ：アヤが服を袋に入れて衣料品店の回収ボックスに入れ、店員から割引券をもらっている。／3コマめ：アヤがその割引券を使って新しいセーターを買っている。
steps.model: One day, Aya was cleaning her room. She found many clothes that were too small for her. She put them in a bag and took them to a clothing store that collected old clothes. The clerk gave her a discount coupon. Later, she used the coupon to buy a new sweater. She was glad that her old clothes would be used again.
steps.hint: 「One day, Aya was cleaning her room.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that people buy too many clothes these days. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「最近の人々は服を買いすぎている」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. Clothes are cheap these days, so people buy new ones easily. Also, many people throw away clothes after wearing them only a few times.
steps.hint: I agree. / I disagree. と立場を言ってから、because で理由を続けよう。

steps.q: Do you think it is a good idea to buy secondhand clothes?
steps.ja: 古着を買うのはよい考えだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Secondhand clothes are cheaper than new ones. Also, buying them helps reduce waste, so it is good for the environment.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. と答えてから、理由を2つ言おう。

cards.title: Robots in Nursing Homes
cards.passage: In Japan, there are not enough workers at nursing homes. To solve this problem, some nursing homes have started to use robots. These robots help workers lift elderly people or talk with residents. By doing so, they can reduce the workers' burden. However, some people think that robots cannot take care of people as kindly as humans.
cards.ja: 日本では介護施設の働き手が足りません。この問題を解決するために、ロボットを使い始めた介護施設もあります。これらのロボットは、職員がお年寄りを持ち上げるのを手伝ったり、入居者と話をしたりします。そうすることで、職員の負担を減らすことができます。しかし、ロボットは人間ほど優しく人の世話はできないと考える人もいます。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can robots reduce the workers' burden?
steps.ja: 文章によると、ロボットはどのようにして職員の負担を減らすことができますか。
steps.model: By helping workers lift elderly people and talking with residents.
steps.hint: By ...ing の形で、「そうすることで(By doing so)」の前の文を使おう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Nana visited her grandmother at a nursing home."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Nana visited her grandmother at a nursing home.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：ナナが介護施設のおばあさんを訪ねると、おばあさんが小さなロボットと話している。／2コマめ：ナナとおばあさんとロボットが一緒に歌を歌っている。／3コマめ：帰り道、ナナが母親に「ロボットを作るエンジニアになりたい」と話している。
steps.model: One day, Nana visited her grandmother at a nursing home. When she arrived, her grandmother was talking with a small robot. Then Nana, her grandmother, and the robot sang songs together, and they had a lot of fun. On the way home, Nana told her mother that she wanted to become an engineer and build robots in the future.
steps.hint: 「One day, Nana visited her grandmother at a nursing home.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that robots will be used in more homes in the future. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「将来、より多くの家庭でロボットが使われる」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I think so. Robots can do housework such as cleaning and cooking. Also, they can help elderly people who live alone, so many families will want them.
steps.hint: まず I agree. か I disagree. を言い、理由を2つ（Also, ...）挙げよう。

steps.q: Do you think nursing care is an important job for society?
steps.ja: 介護は社会にとって大切な仕事だと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. The number of elderly people is increasing, and many of them need help in daily life. Also, care workers support families who are too busy to look after their parents.
steps.hint: Yes. か No. のあと、For example, ... で具体例を入れよう。

cards.title: E-books
cards.passage: Electronic books, or e-books, are becoming more popular. People can carry hundreds of books in one small device. Some e-book readers allow users to change the size of the letters. In this way, people with poor eyesight can read books more comfortably. However, many people still prefer paper books because they like the feeling of turning pages.
cards.ja: 電子書籍は人気が高まっています。人々は小さな端末1つに何百冊もの本を入れて持ち歩けます。文字の大きさを変えられる電子書籍リーダーもあります。このようにして、視力が弱い人もより快適に本を読むことができます。しかし、ページをめくる感覚が好きなので、今でも紙の本を好む人がたくさんいます。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can people with poor eyesight read books more comfortably?
steps.ja: 文章によると、視力が弱い人はどのようにしてより快適に本を読むことができますか。
steps.model: By changing the size of the letters on e-book readers.
steps.hint: 「このようにして(In this way)」の前の文を見て、By ...ing で答えよう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Taku was packing for a trip."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Taku was packing for a trip.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：タクが旅行の準備をしていて、たくさんの本でかばんが重くなり、閉まらない。／2コマめ：父親がタクにタブレットを見せて、電子書籍を何冊もダウンロードしている。／3コマめ：飛行機の中で、タクがタブレットで本を読んでいる。
steps.model: One day, Taku was packing for a trip. He wanted to take many books, but his bag became too heavy and would not close. His father showed him a tablet and helped him download several e-books. Taku took out the paper books and packed the tablet instead. On the plane, he enjoyed reading the books on his tablet.
steps.hint: 「One day, Taku was packing for a trip.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that paper books will disappear in the future. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「将来、紙の本はなくなる」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I disagree. Many people like the feeling of holding paper books. Also, reading paper books is easier on our eyes than looking at screens for a long time.
steps.hint: I think ... / I don't think ... で始めて、because のあとに理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think schools should use digital textbooks instead of paper ones?
steps.ja: 学校は紙の教科書の代わりにデジタル教科書を使うべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Students do not need to carry heavy bags to school. Also, digital textbooks can show videos and play sounds, so they help students understand lessons better.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. を言ってから、because ... と Also, ... で理由をつなげよう。

cards.title: Disaster Drills
cards.passage: Japan has many natural disasters such as earthquakes and typhoons. It is important for people to know what to do when a disaster happens. Many schools and towns hold disaster drills every year. By doing so, people can learn where to go and how to act calmly in an emergency. Some families also keep emergency bags with food and water at home.
cards.ja: 日本では地震や台風などの自然災害が多くあります。災害が起きたときに何をすべきか知っておくことは大切です。多くの学校や町が毎年防災訓練を行っています。そうすることで、人々は緊急時にどこへ行き、どう落ち着いて行動すればよいかを学ぶことができます。食料や水を入れた非常用バッグを家に置いている家族もいます。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can people learn where to go and how to act calmly in an emergency?
steps.ja: 文章によると、人々はどのようにして、緊急時にどこへ行き、どう落ち着いて行動すればよいかを学ぶことができますか。
steps.model: By taking part in disaster drills every year.
steps.hint: By ...ing の形で、「そうすることで(By doing so)」の前の文を使おう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Mrs. Ono and her son were watching the news."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Mrs. Ono and her son were watching the news.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：小野さんと息子がテレビで台風のニュースを見ている。／2コマめ：二人がスーパーで水や缶詰、電池を買っている。／3コマめ：家で、二人が買ったものを非常用バッグに入れている。
steps.model: One day, Mrs. Ono and her son were watching the news on TV. They learned that a big typhoon was coming. They went to the supermarket and bought water, canned food, and batteries. When they got home, they put the things they had bought into an emergency bag. They felt ready for the typhoon.
steps.hint: 「One day, Mrs. Ono and her son were watching the news.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that schools should teach students more about disasters. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「学校は生徒に災害についてもっと教えるべきだ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. Students spend a lot of time at school, so they need to know what to do if a disaster happens there. Also, they can share what they learned with their families.
steps.hint: I agree. / I disagree. と立場を言ってから、because で理由を続けよう。

steps.q: Do you think people in Japan are well prepared for natural disasters?
steps.ja: 日本の人々は自然災害への備えが十分にできていると思いますか。
steps.model: No. Many people do not keep enough food and water at home. Also, some people do not know where the nearest shelter is, so they should check it.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. と答えてから、理由を2つ言おう。

cards.title: Solar Panels
cards.passage: More homes in Japan are putting solar panels on their roofs. Solar panels make electricity from sunlight, so families can use less electricity from power companies. Some local governments give money to people who buy solar panels. In this way, they help more families use clean energy. However, solar panels do not work well on cloudy or rainy days.
cards.ja: 日本では屋根に太陽光パネルを取り付ける家が増えています。太陽光パネルは日光から電気を作るので、家族は電力会社からの電気を使う量を減らせます。太陽光パネルを買う人にお金を出す自治体もあります。このようにして、より多くの家族がクリーンなエネルギーを使えるよう手助けしています。しかし、曇りや雨の日には太陽光パネルはあまりうまく働きません。

steps.q: According to the passage, how do some local governments help more families use clean energy?
steps.ja: 文章によると、一部の自治体はどのようにして、より多くの家族がクリーンなエネルギーを使えるよう手助けしていますか。
steps.model: By giving money to people who buy solar panels.
steps.hint: 「このようにして(In this way)」の前の文を見て、By ...ing で答えよう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Mr. Ueda was looking at his electricity bill."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Mr. Ueda was looking at his electricity bill.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：上田さんが電気代の請求書を見て驚いている。／2コマめ：作業員が上田さんの家の屋根に太陽光パネルを取り付けている。／3コマめ：数か月後、上田さんが安くなった請求書を見て家族と喜んでいる。
steps.model: One day, Mr. Ueda was looking at his electricity bill. He was surprised because it was very expensive. He decided to put solar panels on the roof of his house, and some workers came to set them up. A few months later, Mr. Ueda looked at his new bill. It was much cheaper, and his family was very happy.
steps.hint: 「One day, Mr. Ueda was looking at his electricity bill.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that people should try harder to save electricity at home. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「人々は家でもっと節電に努めるべきだ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. Producing electricity often creates gases that are bad for the environment. Also, if people save electricity, they can pay less money every month.
steps.hint: まず I agree. か I disagree. を言い、理由を2つ（Also, ...）挙げよう。

steps.q: Do you think Japan should use more natural energy such as solar and wind power?
steps.ja: 日本は太陽光や風力のような自然エネルギーをもっと使うべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Natural energy does not run out, and it does not cause much pollution. Also, Japan buys a lot of oil from other countries, so natural energy can help Japan save money.
steps.hint: Yes. か No. のあと、For example, ... で具体例を入れよう。

cards.title: Dogs in Hospitals
cards.passage: Some hospitals have started a program in which trained dogs visit patients. Many patients feel relaxed when they touch the dogs. Doctors say that spending time with animals can reduce stress. By doing so, patients may become more positive about their treatment. However, hospitals must keep the dogs clean so that patients do not get sick.
cards.ja: 訓練を受けた犬が患者を訪問するプログラムを始めた病院もあります。多くの患者は犬にさわるとリラックスします。医師によると、動物と過ごすことでストレスが減ることがあります。そうすることで、患者は治療に前向きになるかもしれません。しかし、患者が病気にならないよう、病院は犬を清潔に保たなければなりません。

steps.q: According to the passage, how may patients become more positive about their treatment?
steps.ja: 文章によると、患者はどのようにして治療に前向きになるかもしれませんか。
steps.model: By spending time with animals.
steps.hint: By ...ing の形で、「そうすることで(By doing so)」の前の文を使おう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Rina was in the hospital because she had broken her leg."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Rina was in the hospital because she had broken her leg.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：足を骨折したリナが病院のベッドでつまらなそうにしている。／2コマめ：訓練された犬が病室に来て、リナが笑顔で犬をなでている。／3コマめ：退院の日、リナが犬に手をふって、松葉づえで歩いている。
steps.model: One day, Rina was in the hospital because she had broken her leg. She felt bored and sad in her bed. Then a trained dog visited her room. Rina smiled and touched the dog gently, and she felt much better. On the day she left the hospital, she waved goodbye to the dog and walked out with crutches.
steps.hint: 「One day, Rina was in the hospital because she had broken her leg.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that keeping a pet is good for children. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「ペットを飼うことは子どもにとってよいことだ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. Children can learn to be responsible by taking care of a pet every day. Also, pets can make children feel happy when they are lonely.
steps.hint: I think ... / I don't think ... で始めて、because のあとに理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think more places should allow people to bring their pets?
steps.ja: ペットを連れて入れる場所をもっと増やすべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: No. Some people are afraid of animals or have allergies. Also, pets may make noise or leave hair, so they can cause problems for others.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. を言ってから、because ... と Also, ... で理由をつなげよう。

cards.title: Cooking Classes for Children
cards.passage: These days, cooking classes for children are becoming popular. In these classes, children learn how to use knives safely and make simple dishes. They also learn about the nutrition of different foods. In this way, they can develop healthy eating habits. Some parents say their children have started to eat vegetables they did not like before.
cards.ja: 近ごろ、子ども向けの料理教室が人気になっています。こうした教室では、子どもたちは包丁を安全に使う方法や簡単な料理の作り方を学びます。また、さまざまな食べ物の栄養についても学びます。このようにして、健康的な食習慣を身につけることができます。以前は嫌いだった野菜を子どもが食べるようになったと言う親もいます。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can children develop healthy eating habits?
steps.ja: 文章によると、子どもたちはどのようにして健康的な食習慣を身につけることができますか。
steps.model: By learning about the nutrition of different foods.
steps.hint: 「このようにして(In this way)」の前の文を見て、By ...ing で答えよう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Sota did not want to eat his carrots at dinner."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Sota did not want to eat his carrots at dinner.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：夕食で、ソウタがお皿のにんじんを残してしかめっつらをしている。／2コマめ：週末、ソウタが料理教室でにんじんのケーキを作っている。／3コマめ：家で、ソウタが自分で作ったにんじんケーキを家族にふるまっている。
steps.model: One day, Sota did not want to eat his carrots at dinner. His mother was worried about him. On the weekend, he went to a cooking class for children and made a carrot cake. He was surprised that it tasted very good. When he got home, he made the cake again and served it to his family. Everyone enjoyed it.
steps.hint: 「One day, Sota did not want to eat his carrots at dinner.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that children should help their parents cook at home. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「子どもは家で親の料理を手伝うべきだ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. Children can learn useful skills for the future by cooking. Also, parents are busy, so it is helpful if children do some housework.
steps.hint: I agree. / I disagree. と立場を言ってから、because で理由を続けよう。

steps.q: Do you think people today eat a healthy diet?
steps.ja: 今の人々は健康的な食事をしていると思いますか。
steps.model: No. Many people eat fast food or instant food because they are busy. Also, some young people skip breakfast, so they do not get enough nutrition.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. と答えてから、理由を2つ言おう。

cards.title: Farmers' Markets
cards.passage: Farmers' markets are held in many towns on weekends. At these markets, farmers sell vegetables and fruit directly to customers. Customers can buy fresh food and ask farmers how it was grown. By doing so, they can feel safe about what they eat. Farmers can also earn more money because they do not need to pay stores to sell their products.
cards.ja: 多くの町で週末にファーマーズマーケットが開かれています。こうした市場では、農家が野菜や果物を直接お客さんに売ります。お客さんは新鮮な食べ物を買い、それがどのように育てられたかを農家にたずねることができます。そうすることで、食べるものについて安心できます。農家も、商品を売ってもらうためにお店にお金を払う必要がないので、より多くのお金をかせげます。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can customers feel safe about what they eat?
steps.ja: 文章によると、お客さんはどのようにして食べるものについて安心できますか。
steps.model: By asking farmers how the food was grown.
steps.hint: By ...ing の形で、「そうすることで(By doing so)」の前の文を使おう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Hina and her mother went to a farmers' market."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Hina and her mother went to a farmers' market.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：ヒナと母親がファーマーズマーケットで、農家の人からいちごを買っている。／2コマめ：農家の人が二人に畑の写真を見せて、いちごの育て方を説明している。／3コマめ：家で、ヒナと母親がいちごでジャムを作っている。
steps.model: One day, Hina and her mother went to a farmers' market. They bought some strawberries from a farmer. The farmer showed them pictures of his field and explained how he grew the strawberries. Hina found it very interesting. When they got home, Hina and her mother used the strawberries to make jam.
steps.hint: 「One day, Hina and her mother went to a farmers' market.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that it is better to buy food grown in your own area. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「自分の地域で育てられた食べ物を買うほうがよい」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. Local food is fresh because it does not need to travel far. Also, buying it supports local farmers, so the area becomes more lively.
steps.hint: まず I agree. か I disagree. を言い、理由を2つ（Also, ...）挙げよう。

steps.q: Do you think more young people should become farmers?
steps.ja: もっと多くの若者が農業をするべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Many farmers in Japan are getting old, and there are not enough people to take over their farms. Also, young people can use new technology to make farming easier.
steps.hint: Yes. か No. のあと、For example, ... で具体例を入れよう。

cards.title: Online Museum Tours
cards.passage: Some museums now offer online tours. People can see famous works of art on their computers without leaving home. Guides explain each work through videos. In this way, people who live far away or cannot travel easily can enjoy museums. Some people say, however, that seeing real works of art is a more special experience.
cards.ja: オンラインツアーを提供している美術館もあります。人々は家から出ずに、パソコンで有名な美術作品を見ることができます。ガイドが動画でそれぞれの作品を説明します。このようにして、遠くに住む人や簡単に旅行できない人も美術館を楽しむことができます。しかし、本物の作品を見るほうがより特別な経験だと言う人もいます。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can people who live far away enjoy museums?
steps.ja: 文章によると、遠くに住む人はどのようにして美術館を楽しむことができますか。
steps.model: By taking online tours on their computers.
steps.hint: 「このようにして(In this way)」の前の文を見て、By ...ing で答えよう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Kaito's grandfather wanted to see a famous painting."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Kaito's grandfather wanted to see a famous painting.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：足をけがしたおじいさんが、新聞で遠くの美術館の展示の記事を見て残念そうにしている。／2コマめ：カイトがパソコンで美術館のオンラインツアーを開き、おじいさんと一緒に見ている。／3コマめ：数か月後、足が治ったおじいさんとカイトが本物の美術館で同じ絵を見ている。
steps.model: One day, Kaito's grandfather wanted to see a famous painting at a museum, but he had hurt his leg and could not travel. Kaito found an online tour of the museum and showed it to him on his computer. They watched it together and enjoyed it. A few months later, his grandfather's leg got better, and they went to see the real painting together.
steps.hint: 「One day, Kaito's grandfather wanted to see a famous painting.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that museums should be free for everyone. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「美術館は誰でも無料にすべきだ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. If museums are free, more people can learn about art and history. Also, families with children can visit them more often, so children will become interested in art.
steps.hint: I think ... / I don't think ... で始めて、because のあとに理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think students should go on more school trips to museums?
steps.ja: 生徒はもっと美術館や博物館への校外学習に行くべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Students can learn things that they cannot learn from textbooks. Also, seeing real objects makes them more interested in history and art.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. を言ってから、because ... と Also, ... で理由をつなげよう。

cards.title: Studying Abroad
cards.passage: Studying abroad can be a valuable experience for young people. Students can improve their language skills and learn about different cultures. However, studying abroad costs a lot of money. Some universities offer scholarships to students who want to study in other countries. By doing so, they give more students the chance to have this experience.
cards.ja: 留学は若者にとって貴重な経験になりえます。学生は語学力を伸ばし、異なる文化について学ぶことができます。しかし、留学には多くのお金がかかります。外国で学びたい学生に奨学金を出す大学もあります。そうすることで、より多くの学生にこの経験をする機会を与えています。

steps.q: According to the passage, how do some universities give more students the chance to study abroad?
steps.ja: 文章によると、一部の大学はどのようにして、より多くの学生に留学の機会を与えていますか。
steps.model: By offering scholarships to students who want to study in other countries.
steps.hint: By ...ing の形で、「そうすることで(By doing so)」の前の文を使おう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Miku saw a poster about a scholarship."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Miku saw a poster about a scholarship.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：ミクが大学の掲示板で「留学奨学金」のポスターを見ている。／2コマめ：ミクが夜遅くまで英語を勉強して、申込書を書いている。／3コマめ：数か月後、ミクが外国の大学で、いろいろな国の学生と話している。
steps.model: One day, Miku saw a poster about a scholarship. It was for students who wanted to study abroad, and she was very interested in it. She studied English hard until late at night and filled out the application form. A few months later, she was studying at a university in another country. She enjoyed talking with students from many different countries.
steps.hint: 「One day, Miku saw a poster about a scholarship.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that it is necessary to study abroad to speak English well. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「英語を上手に話すには留学が必要だ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I disagree. Today, students can talk with people in other countries on the internet. Also, there are many English schools and apps in Japan, so people can practice without going abroad.
steps.hint: I agree. / I disagree. と立場を言ってから、because で理由を続けよう。

steps.q: Do you think more Japanese students will study abroad in the future?
steps.ja: 将来、留学する日本の学生は増えると思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Many companies want workers who can work with people from other countries. Also, there are more scholarships now, so it is easier for students to go abroad.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. と答えてから、理由を2つ言おう。

cards.title: Repair Cafés
cards.passage: When things break, many people simply throw them away and buy new ones. However, events called repair cafés are appearing in some communities. At these events, volunteers with special skills help people fix broken items such as toys, lamps and clothes. In this way, people can use their things for a longer time. They can also learn how to repair things themselves.
cards.ja: 物が壊れると、多くの人はそれを捨てて新しい物を買ってしまいます。しかし、一部の地域ではリペアカフェと呼ばれるイベントが登場しています。こうしたイベントでは、特別な技術を持つボランティアが、おもちゃやランプ、服などの壊れた物を直す手伝いをします。このようにして、人々は物をより長く使うことができます。また、自分で物を直す方法も学べます。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can people use their things for a longer time?
steps.ja: 文章によると、人々はどのようにして物をより長く使うことができますか。
steps.model: Because volunteers help them fix broken items at repair cafés.
steps.hint: In this way の前の文を見て、Because volunteers help them ... と答えよう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Ren's favorite toy robot broke."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Ren's favorite toy robot broke.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：レンのお気に入りのおもちゃのロボットのうでがとれて、レンが泣いている。／2コマめ：レンと父親が公民館のリペアカフェで、ボランティアのおじいさんにおもちゃを直してもらっている。／3コマめ：家で、レンが道具を使って自分で古い時計を直している。
steps.model: One day, Ren's favorite toy robot broke, and he started crying. His father took him to a repair café at the community center. A volunteer fixed the toy and showed Ren how he did it. Ren became interested in repairing things. A few weeks later, he used some tools to fix an old clock at home by himself.
steps.hint: 「One day, Ren's favorite toy robot broke.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that it is better to repair things than to buy new ones. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「新しい物を買うより修理するほうがよい」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. Repairing things can save money. Also, it reduces the amount of garbage, so it is good for the environment.
steps.hint: まず I agree. か I disagree. を言い、理由を2つ（Also, ...）挙げよう。

steps.q: Do you think students should learn how to repair things at school?
steps.ja: 生徒は学校で物の直し方を学ぶべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Knowing how to repair things is a useful skill in daily life. Also, students will learn to take care of their things, so they will not waste them.
steps.hint: Yes. か No. のあと、For example, ... で具体例を入れよう。

cards.title: Buses in Rural Areas
cards.passage: In many rural areas, the number of buses has been decreasing. This is a serious problem for elderly people who do not drive. Some towns have started a service in which small buses come when people call them. By doing so, elderly people can go shopping or to the hospital more easily. These services also help towns save money.
cards.ja: 多くの地方では、バスの本数が減ってきています。これは車を運転しないお年寄りにとって深刻な問題です。人々が電話で呼ぶと小型バスが来てくれるサービスを始めた町もあります。そうすることで、お年寄りは買い物や病院により行きやすくなります。こうしたサービスは町がお金を節約するのにも役立っています。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can elderly people go shopping or to the hospital more easily?
steps.ja: 文章によると、お年寄りはどのようにして買い物や病院により行きやすくなりますか。
steps.model: By calling small buses that come when people need them.
steps.hint: By ...ing の形で、「そうすることで(By doing so)」の前の文を使おう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Mrs. Kimura needed to go to the hospital."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Mrs. Kimura needed to go to the hospital.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：木村さん（おばあさん）がバス停の時刻表を見て、次のバスが3時間後だと知り困っている。／2コマめ：木村さんが家から電話をかけて、小型バスを呼んでいる。／3コマめ：小型バスが家の前に来て、運転手が木村さんが乗るのを手伝っている。
steps.model: One day, Mrs. Kimura needed to go to the hospital. When she checked the timetable at the bus stop, she found that the next bus would not come for three hours. She went back home and called a small bus service on the phone. Soon, a small bus came to her house, and the driver helped her get on. She arrived at the hospital on time.
steps.hint: 「One day, Mrs. Kimura needed to go to the hospital.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that elderly people should stop driving at a certain age. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「お年寄りはある年齢になったら運転をやめるべきだ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I disagree. Some elderly people are still good drivers. Also, in rural areas, people cannot go shopping without a car, so life would be very difficult for them.
steps.hint: I think ... / I don't think ... で始めて、because のあとに理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think it is better to live in a city than in the countryside?
steps.ja: 田舎より都市に住むほうがよいと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Cities have many stores, hospitals, and trains, so life is convenient. Also, there are more jobs in cities, so it is easier to find work.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. を言ってから、because ... と Also, ... で理由をつなげよう。

cards.title: Coaches for School Clubs
cards.passage: In Japan, many teachers are very busy because they have to lead club activities after school. To solve this problem, some schools have started to ask local sports coaches to teach club activities. By doing so, teachers can spend more time preparing for their classes. Students can also learn skills from experienced coaches.
cards.ja: 日本では、放課後に部活動を指導しなければならないため、多くの先生がとても忙しくしています。この問題を解決するために、地域のスポーツコーチに部活動の指導を頼み始めた学校もあります。そうすることで、先生は授業の準備により多くの時間を使えます。生徒も経験豊かなコーチから技術を学ぶことができます。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can teachers spend more time preparing for their classes?
steps.ja: 文章によると、先生はどのようにして授業の準備により多くの時間を使えますか。
steps.model: By asking local sports coaches to teach club activities.
steps.hint: By ...ing の形で、「そうすることで(By doing so)」の前の文を使おう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, a new coach came to the school's basketball club."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, a new coach came to the school's basketball club.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：バスケットボール部に地域の新しいコーチが来て、部員にあいさつしている。／2コマめ：コーチがショウ（男子生徒）にシュートの打ち方を教えている。／3コマめ：試合で、ショウがシュートを決めて、チームのみんなが喜んでいる。
steps.model: One day, a new coach came to the school's basketball club. He was from the local community, and he introduced himself to the members. During practice, he taught Sho how to shoot the ball better. Sho practiced hard every day. At the next game, Sho made an important shot, and all his teammates were very happy.
steps.hint: 「One day, a new coach came to the school's basketball club.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that club activities are more important than studying for students. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「生徒にとって部活動は勉強より大切だ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I disagree. Club activities are fun, but students need to study to prepare for their future. However, club activities can teach teamwork, so students should do both.
steps.hint: I agree. / I disagree. と立場を言ってから、because で理由を続けよう。

steps.q: Do you think students should be able to choose not to join club activities?
steps.ja: 生徒は部活動に入らないことを選べるべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Some students want to spend their time on other things, such as studying or helping their families. Also, if they are forced to join, they will not enjoy it.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. と答えてから、理由を2つ言おう。

cards.title: Trees in Cities
cards.passage: In summer, cities become much hotter than the countryside. This is because buildings and roads store heat. Some cities are planting more trees along streets and on the roofs of buildings. In this way, they can lower the temperature and make the city more comfortable. Trees also give birds and insects places to live.
cards.ja: 夏、都市は田舎よりずっと暑くなります。これは建物や道路が熱をためこむからです。通り沿いや建物の屋上に木を増やしている都市もあります。このようにして、気温を下げ、都市をより過ごしやすくすることができます。木は鳥や虫に住む場所も与えてくれます。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can some cities lower the temperature?
steps.ja: 文章によると、一部の都市はどのようにして気温を下げることができますか。
steps.model: By planting more trees along streets and on the roofs of buildings.
steps.hint: 「このようにして(In this way)」の前の文を見て、By ...ing で答えよう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, the students in Ms. Hara's class were talking about the hot summer."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, the students in Ms. Hara's class were talking about the hot summer.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：暑い教室で、原先生のクラスの生徒たちが汗をかきながら話し合っている。／2コマめ：生徒たちが地域の人たちと一緒に校庭に木を植えている。／3コマめ：数年後、大きくなった木の下で生徒たちが涼しそうにお弁当を食べている。
steps.model: One day, the students in Ms. Hara's class were talking about the hot summer. They decided to do something to make their school cooler. They planted some trees in the schoolyard with people from the community. A few years later, the trees had grown tall. The students enjoyed eating lunch in the cool shade under the trees.
steps.hint: 「One day, the students in Ms. Hara's class were talking about the hot summer.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that people should spend more time in nature. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「人々はもっと自然の中で時間を過ごすべきだ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I agree. Spending time in nature helps people relax and reduce stress. Also, children can learn about plants and animals by playing outside.
steps.hint: まず I agree. か I disagree. を言い、理由を2つ（Also, ...）挙げよう。

steps.q: Do you think global warming is a serious problem?
steps.ja: 地球温暖化は深刻な問題だと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. Summers are getting hotter every year, and many people get sick because of the heat. Also, strong typhoons and heavy rain are causing more damage.
steps.hint: Yes. か No. のあと、For example, ... で具体例を入れよう。

cards.title: Reusable Bottles
cards.passage: Many people buy drinks in plastic bottles every day. However, some cities have set up free water stations in parks and train stations. People can fill their own bottles with water at these stations. By doing so, they can reduce the number of plastic bottles they throw away. Some shops also give discounts to customers who bring their own cups.
cards.ja: 多くの人が毎日ペットボトルの飲み物を買っています。しかし、公園や駅に無料の給水所を設けた都市もあります。人々はそこで自分のボトルに水を入れることができます。そうすることで、捨てるペットボトルの数を減らすことができます。自分のカップを持ってきたお客さんに割引をするお店もあります。

steps.q: According to the passage, how can people reduce the number of plastic bottles they throw away?
steps.ja: 文章によると、人々はどのようにして捨てるペットボトルの数を減らすことができますか。
steps.model: By filling their own bottles with water at water stations.
steps.hint: By ...ing の形で、「そうすることで(By doing so)」の前の文を使おう。

steps.q: Now, please look at the three pictures and tell the story. You have two minutes. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Kota was going to play soccer in the park."
steps.ja: 3つの絵を見て、お話をしてください。最初の文は「One day, Kota was going to play soccer in the park.」です。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：コウタがサッカーの練習に行く前に、母親が水筒を渡している。／2コマめ：練習のあと、コウタが公園の給水所で水筒に水を入れている。／3コマめ：友達もそれを見て、次の練習に自分の水筒を持ってきている。
steps.model: One day, Kota was going to play soccer in the park. Before he left, his mother gave him a water bottle. After practice, his bottle was empty, so he filled it at a free water station in the park. His friends saw him and thought it was a good idea. At the next practice, they all brought their own bottles.
steps.hint: 「One day, Kota was going to play soccer in the park.」で始めて、1コマずつ過去形で説明しよう。

steps.q: Some people say that shops should stop selling drinks in plastic bottles. What do you think about that?
steps.ja: 「お店はペットボトル入りの飲み物を売るのをやめるべきだ」と言う人がいます。あなたはどう思いますか。
steps.model: I disagree. Plastic bottles are light and easy to carry, so they are useful when people are outside. Instead, people should recycle bottles properly.
steps.hint: I think ... / I don't think ... で始めて、because のあとに理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think people should carry their own water bottles?
steps.ja: 人々は自分の水筒を持ち歩くべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes. It helps reduce plastic waste. Also, people can save money because they do not need to buy drinks every day.
steps.hint: Yes. / No. を言ってから、because ... と Also, ... で理由をつなげよう。

gp1.title: 準1級 スピーキングテスト
gp1.howto: 4コマの絵を見て物語を話し、そのあと絵や社会の話題についての質問に答えます。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Yui and her father were walking past an empty lot in their neighborhood." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、ユイと父親は近所の空き地のそばを歩いていました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Yui and her father were walking past an empty lot in their neighborhood. Her father said that it would be nice to turn the lot into a garden. That weekend, many neighbors gathered there. They pulled out the weeds and dug the soil together. A few months later, the vegetables had grown well, and Yui and the other children were picking tomatoes happily. However, one morning, when Yui went to the garden, she found that birds had eaten some of the vegetables. She looked very disappointed.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：ユイと父親が雑草だらけの空き地を見て、父親が「ここを畑にしたら？」と話している。／2コマめ：週末、近所の人たちが集まり、草を抜いて土を耕している。／3コマめ：数か月後、野菜が育ち、ユイと近所の子どもたちがトマトを収穫している。／4コマめ：ある朝、ユイが畑に行くと、野菜の一部が鳥に食べられていて、がっかりしている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Yui, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがユイだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that it is sad that the birds ate our vegetables, but we can put up a net to protect the garden next time.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think more people should grow their own vegetables?
steps.ja: もっと多くの人が自分で野菜を育てるべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Growing vegetables teaches people where food comes from, and fresh vegetables from your own garden are healthy. Also, it is a good way to relax after work or school.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should local governments do more to create green spaces in cities?
steps.ja: 地方自治体は都市の緑地を増やすためにもっと取り組むべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think they should. Parks and gardens make cities cooler in summer and give people a place to exercise. For example, children can play safely and older people can meet their neighbors.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Kenta's teacher announced that every student would get a tablet computer." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、ケンタの先生は、生徒全員がタブレット端末をもらえると発表しました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Kenta's teacher announced that every student would get a tablet computer. The students were very excited. In class, Kenta and his classmates used their tablets to look up information, and they prepared a group presentation together. That night, however, Kenta watched videos on his tablet until very late. His mother looked worried when she saw him. The next morning, Kenta was so sleepy that he yawned during class, and his teacher looked troubled.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：教室で先生がタブレットを見せながら発表し、生徒たちが喜んでいる。／2コマめ：授業中、ケンタたちがタブレットで調べものをして、グループで発表の準備をしている。／3コマめ：夜、ケンタが自分の部屋でタブレットの動画を夜遅くまで見ていて、母親が心配そうにドアから見ている。／4コマめ：翌朝、ケンタが授業中に眠そうにあくびをしていて、先生が困った顔をしている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Kenta, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがケンタだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that I should not have watched videos so late, and that I need to set a time limit for using my tablet.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think students today spend too much time looking at screens?
steps.ja: 今の生徒は画面を見る時間が長すぎると思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Many students use screens for studying, games, and social media, so they have less time for sports or reading. Also, using screens late at night can make it hard to sleep well.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should schools teach students how to use the Internet safely?
steps.ja: 学校はインターネットを安全に使う方法を教えるべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, they should. Children start using the Internet at a young age, so they need to learn how to protect their personal information. For example, schools can teach them not to share photos with strangers online.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Riko and her friends went to the beach to swim." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、リコと友達は泳ぎに海へ行きました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Riko and her friends went to the beach to swim. When they arrived, they were surprised to see many plastic bottles and pieces of trash on the sand. The next week, they went back with gloves and garbage bags, and they picked up the trash with other volunteers. Later, Riko gave a presentation at school and showed her class pictures of the trash. The next weekend, many more volunteers joined the cleanup. However, Riko saw a man who was about to throw trash on the beach.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：海に着いたリコたちが、砂浜にたくさんのペットボトルやごみが落ちているのを見て驚いている。／2コマめ：翌週、リコたちが手袋とごみ袋を持って、ほかのボランティアと一緒にごみを拾っている。／3コマめ：学校で、リコがごみの写真を見せながらクラスで発表している。／4コマめ：次の週末、ボランティアの数がとても増えているが、一人の男性が砂浜にまたごみを捨てようとしているのをリコが見ている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Riko, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがリコだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that it is disappointing to see someone throwing trash, so I would politely ask him to take it home.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think young people today are interested in environmental problems?
steps.ja: 今の若者は環境問題に関心があると思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think many young people are interested. They learn about climate change and plastic pollution at school and on the Internet. For example, some students join cleanup events or try to use less plastic in daily life.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should companies be responsible for reducing plastic waste?
steps.ja: 企業はプラスチックごみを減らす責任を負うべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Companies produce most of the plastic packaging, so they have the power to change it. If they use paper or reusable containers instead, the amount of waste will decrease a lot.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Sota's grandmother bought a smartphone." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、ソウタの祖母はスマートフォンを買いました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Sota's grandmother bought a smartphone. However, when she opened the box, she did not know how to use it. So Sota sat next to her and taught her how to send messages and make video calls. A few weeks later, his grandmother was enjoying a video call with a friend who lived far away. She was laughing happily. But at dinner one evening, she was looking at her smartphone the whole time and did not notice when Sota and his mother spoke to her.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：祖母が新しいスマートフォンの箱を開けて、使い方が分からず困っている。／2コマめ：ソウタが祖母の隣に座り、メッセージやビデオ通話の使い方を教えている。／3コマめ：数週間後、祖母が遠くに住む友達とビデオ通話をして楽しそうに笑っている。／4コマめ：夕食のとき、祖母がスマートフォンばかり見ていて、ソウタと母親が話しかけても気づかない。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Sota, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがソウタだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that I am glad she enjoys her smartphone, but I hope she will put it away during dinner.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think older people should learn to use new technology?
steps.ja: 高齢者は新しい技術の使い方を学ぶべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think they should. New technology can make their lives easier and safer. For example, they can shop online, check their health, and stay in touch with family members who live far away.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Is it a good idea for families to have rules about smartphone use at home?
steps.ja: 家庭でスマートフォンの使い方にルールを作るのはよい考えですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think it is a good idea. If family members use their phones all the time, they talk with each other less. Rules such as no phones at dinner can help families spend quality time together.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Mai's father started working from home." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、マイの父親は在宅勤務を始めました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Mai's father started working from home. He had an online meeting in the living room while Mai and her little brother were playing nearby. During the meeting, her brother shouted loudly, and their father looked troubled. That weekend, the whole family worked together to clean up an empty room and turned it into an office for him. After that, he could work quietly in his new office. However, Mai was waiting outside the door with a board game, and she looked lonely.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：父親がリビングでパソコンを開いてオンライン会議をしていて、マイと弟が近くで遊んでいる。／2コマめ：会議中に弟が大声を出し、父親が困った顔をしている。／3コマめ：週末、家族で協力して空き部屋を片付け、父親用の仕事部屋を作っている。／4コマめ：父親が新しい仕事部屋で働いていて、ボードゲームを持ったマイがドアの外でさびしそうに待っている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Mai's father, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがマイの父親だったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that I should take a short break to play with Mai, and that I will spend more time with her after work.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think more companies will allow their workers to work from home in the future?
steps.ja: 将来、在宅勤務を認める会社は増えると思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Because of the Internet, many jobs can be done anywhere. Working from home also saves time spent commuting, so companies may find that their workers are happier and more productive.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should parents spend more time with their children even if they are busy with work?
steps.ja: 親は仕事が忙しくても、子どもともっと時間を過ごすべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think they should. Children need attention from their parents to feel safe and loved. Even if parents are busy, they can eat dinner together or talk for a few minutes every day.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Haruto and his family went to a buffet restaurant." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、ハルトと家族はビュッフェレストランに行きました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Haruto and his family went to a buffet restaurant. Haruto put a huge amount of food on his plate, and his mother looked worried. After the meal, there was still a lot of food left on his plate because he could not finish it. Then Haruto saw a staff member throwing the leftover food into a trash can, and he felt sad. The next weekend, at home, Haruto put the leftovers from dinner into a container and stored them in the refrigerator. His mother was surprised.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：ハルトがお皿に料理を山盛りにしていて、母親が心配そうに見ている。／2コマめ：食事の後、ハルトのお皿に食べきれなかった料理がたくさん残っている。／3コマめ：店員が残った料理をごみ箱に捨てているのをハルトが見て、悲しそうな顔をしている。／4コマめ：次の週末、ハルトが家で夕食の残りを容器に入れて冷蔵庫にしまっていて、母親が驚いている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Haruto's mother, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがハルトの母親だったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that I am proud of Haruto because he learned from his experience and is trying not to waste food.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think people in Japan waste too much food?
steps.ja: 日本の人々は食べ物を無駄にしすぎていると思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Supermarkets and restaurants throw away a lot of food that can still be eaten. Also, many families buy more than they need, so food often goes bad in their refrigerators.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should restaurants be required to give their leftover food to people in need?
steps.ja: レストランは余った食べ物を困っている人に提供することを義務づけられるべきですか。
steps.model: I think it is a good idea, but it should not be required. Restaurants must make sure the food is safe, so it can be difficult. However, if the government supports food banks, more restaurants will be able to donate food.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Aoi saw a sign about a new bike-sharing service at the station." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、アオイは駅で新しいシェアサイクルのサービスの看板を見ました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Aoi saw a sign about a new bike-sharing service at the station. She told her friend about it, and they decided to try it. They rented bikes and rode around the town happily. When they returned the bikes, however, they noticed that many bikes had been left on the sidewalk or had fallen over. Then Aoi started to move the bikes out of the way because a woman pushing a stroller was waiting and could not pass.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：駅前でアオイが「シェアサイクル始めました」という看板を見ていて、友達に話している。／2コマめ：アオイと友達が自転車を借りて、町の中を楽しそうに走っている。／3コマめ：二人が自転車を返すと、駐輪場の近くに自転車が倒れたり歩道に置きっぱなしになったりしている。／4コマめ：アオイが歩道に置かれた自転車を片付けていて、そこにベビーカーを押した女性が通れずに待っている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Aoi, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがアオイだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that people should be more careful when they park the bikes, because they can cause problems for other people.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think bike-sharing services are good for cities?
steps.ja: シェアサイクルのサービスは都市にとってよいと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think they are. They help reduce traffic and air pollution because people use bikes instead of cars. Also, tourists can easily visit many places, which is good for local shops.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should cities create more bicycle lanes?
steps.ja: 都市は自転車専用レーンをもっと作るべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think they should. In many cities, cyclists have to ride on the road with cars or on the sidewalk with people, which is dangerous. So bicycle lanes would make riding safer for everyone.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Naoki found a poster about a study abroad program at his school." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、ナオキは学校で留学プログラムのポスターを見つけました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Naoki found a poster about a study abroad program at his school. He was very excited and wanted to join. When he got home, he told his parents about it. His mother looked worried, and his father seemed to be thinking carefully. After that, Naoki practiced speaking English with his teacher every day after school. A few months later, he was at the airport waving goodbye to his family. However, he looked a little nervous.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：学校の廊下でナオキが留学プログラムのポスターを見て、わくわくしている。／2コマめ：家でナオキが両親に話していて、母親は心配そうな顔、父親は考えこんでいる。／3コマめ：ナオキが毎日放課後に英語の先生と英会話の練習をしている。／4コマめ：空港でナオキが家族に手を振っているが、少し不安そうな表情をしている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Naoki, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがナオキだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that I am nervous about living in another country, but I am sure it will be a great chance to grow.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think it is necessary to study abroad to become good at English?
steps.ja: 英語が上手になるためには留学が必要だと思いますか。
steps.model: No, I don't think it is necessary. Today, students can use the Internet to talk with people from other countries and watch videos in English. If they study hard every day, they can improve their English in Japan.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should the government give more financial support to students who want to study abroad?
steps.ja: 政府は留学したい学生にもっと経済的な支援をするべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Studying abroad is very expensive, so many students cannot go even if they want to. If the government helps them, more young people can gain international experience and use it in the future.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Emi and her grandfather were walking along the old shopping street in their town." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、エミと祖父は町の古い商店街を歩いていました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Emi and her grandfather were walking along the old shopping street in their town. Many of the shops were closed, and her grandfather sadly talked about how busy the street used to be. Later, Emi discussed ideas for bringing life back to the street with her school friends. That weekend, they held a market on the street, and many families came to enjoy it. After the market, while they were cleaning up, one of the shop owners asked them to hold it every month. Emi looked unsure.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：多くの店がシャッターを閉めていて、祖父がさびしそうに昔の話をしている。／2コマめ：エミが学校の友達と、商店街を元気にするアイデアについて話し合っている。／3コマめ：週末、商店街でエミたちが開いたマーケットに、たくさんの家族が集まっている。／4コマめ：マーケットの後、エミたちが片付けをしていると、店主の一人が「毎月やってほしい」と頼んでいて、エミが困った顔をしている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Emi, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがエミだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that I am happy the market was a success, but holding it every month might be too much work for us students.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think local shopping streets will survive in the future?
steps.ja: 地元の商店街は将来も生き残ると思いますか。
steps.model: I think some of them will survive. Big shopping malls and online shopping are very convenient, so it is hard for small shops. However, if they offer special local products and friendly service, people will still visit them.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should young people be more involved in their local communities?
steps.ja: 若者はもっと地域社会に関わるべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Young people have new ideas and energy that can help their towns. For example, they can join local festivals or volunteer activities, and they can also learn a lot from older people.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Takumi's family received a very high electricity bill." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、タクミの家族はとても高い電気料金の請求書を受け取りました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Takumi's family received a very high electricity bill. His mother was shocked because the lights and the TV were often left on. At a family meeting, Takumi made a poster and explained how they could save electricity. After that, he walked around the house and turned off the lights in empty rooms. On a hot summer day, however, Takumi had turned off the air conditioner, and he was sweating. His grandfather looked tired from the heat.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：母親が電気料金の請求書を見て驚いていて、家の中では電気やテレビがつけっぱなしになっている。／2コマめ：家族会議で、タクミが「使わない電気を消そう」というポスターを作って説明している。／3コマめ：タクミが家の中を回って、誰もいない部屋の電気を消している。／4コマめ：夏の暑い日、タクミがエアコンを切った部屋で汗をかいていて、祖父がぐったりしている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Takumi, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがタクミだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that saving energy is important, but our health is more important, so we should use the air conditioner on hot days.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think people should try harder to save energy in their daily lives?
steps.ja: 人々は日常生活でもっと省エネに努めるべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. If each person saves a little energy, the total amount becomes very large. For example, turning off lights and unplugging machines can reduce both electricity bills and carbon dioxide.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should Japan use more renewable energy, such as solar and wind power?
steps.ja: 日本は太陽光や風力などの再生可能エネルギーをもっと使うべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think it should. Renewable energy does not produce much carbon dioxide, so it helps fight global warming. Also, Japan has to import most of its fuel, so producing its own energy would be safer.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Hina and her parents visited an animal shelter." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、ヒナと両親は動物保護施設を訪れました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Hina and her parents visited an animal shelter. Hina stared at an old dog, and a staff member explained that the dog needed a new home. The family decided to adopt the dog and took it home. Hina gave it food. After that, she got up early every morning and took the dog for a walk. One rainy morning, however, the dog was waiting with its leash in its mouth, but Hina was still in bed and looked sleepy.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：保護施設で、ヒナが一匹の年をとった犬を見つめていて、職員が説明している。／2コマめ：家族がその犬を家に連れて帰り、ヒナがえさをあげている。／3コマめ：毎朝、ヒナが早起きして犬を散歩させている。／4コマめ：雨の日の朝、犬がリードをくわえて待っているが、ヒナはベッドの中で眠そうにしている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Hina, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがヒナだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that I don't want to go out in the rain, but I promised to take care of the dog, so I should get up.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think having a pet is a good way for children to learn responsibility?
steps.ja: ペットを飼うことは、子どもが責任感を学ぶよい方法だと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Pets need food, water, and exercise every day, so children have to take care of them even when they are tired. This experience teaches them that their actions affect other living things.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should pet shops encourage people to adopt animals from shelters?
steps.ja: ペットショップは保護施設から動物を引き取ることを人々に勧めるべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think pet shops should encourage adoption more. Many animals in shelters wait a long time for a new home. If more people adopt pets, fewer animals will be lonely, and shelters will have more space.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Yuto's class visited a local farm." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、ユウトのクラスは地元の農場を訪れました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Yuto's class visited a local farm. A farmer showed them around the fields, and Yuto and his classmates pulled up carrots. A few days later, dishes made with vegetables from that farm were served for school lunch, and Yuto enjoyed eating them. At home, he told his family about the farm while they cooked a meal with local vegetables together. Later, at the supermarket, his mother was trying to choose between cheap imported vegetables and more expensive local ones.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：農家の人がクラスに畑を案内していて、ユウトたちがにんじんを抜いている。／2コマめ：学校の給食に、その農場の野菜を使った料理が出て、ユウトが喜んで食べている。／3コマめ：ユウトが家族に農場の話をしながら、一緒に地元の野菜を使って料理をしている。／4コマめ：スーパーで、母親が安い外国産の野菜と高い地元産の野菜を手に取って迷っていて、ユウトが見ている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Yuto, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがユウトだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that local vegetables are more expensive, but they are fresh and help local farmers, so I would ask my mother to buy them.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think people should buy more food that is produced locally?
steps.ja: 人々は地元で生産された食べ物をもっと買うべきだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Local food is fresh and does not need to be transported far, so it is better for the environment. Also, buying it supports farmers in our area and helps the local economy.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Will the number of young people who want to become farmers increase in the future?
steps.ja: 将来、農家になりたい若者の数は増えるでしょうか。
steps.model: I don't think it will increase much. Farming is hard work and the income is not always stable. However, if new technology such as robots and drones makes farming easier, some young people may become interested.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Saki's school announced that classes would be held online for a week." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、サキの学校は1週間、授業をオンラインで行うと発表しました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Saki's school announced that classes would be held online for a week. At first, Saki enjoyed taking lessons on her computer at home. A few days later, however, her Internet connection stopped working, and she was in trouble because she could not see the screen. Then she made a video call with her friends, and they did their homework together. When school started again, Saki was very happy to see her friends in the schoolyard. However, one boy was standing alone and looked lonely.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：サキが家の机でパソコンを使ってオンライン授業を受けていて、楽しそうにしている。／2コマめ：数日後、インターネットの接続が切れて画面が止まり、サキが困っている。／3コマめ：サキが友達とビデオ通話をして、一緒に宿題をしている。／4コマめ：学校が再開した日、サキが友達と校庭で再会して喜んでいるが、一人の男の子が離れたところでさびしそうにしている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Saki, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがサキだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that the boy might have had a hard time during the online classes, so I should go and talk to him.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think online classes are as effective as classes in a classroom?
steps.ja: オンライン授業は教室での授業と同じくらい効果的だと思いますか。
steps.model: No, I don't think so. In a classroom, students can ask questions easily and learn from their classmates. Online, it is easy to lose concentration, and some students do not have a good Internet connection.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should schools continue to use online lessons even when students can come to school?
steps.ja: 生徒が登校できるときでも、学校はオンライン授業を続けるべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think schools should use them sometimes. For example, students who are sick or live far away can still join classes. Also, online lessons can connect students with experts or schools in other countries.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Ren's town held an earthquake drill." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、レンの町は地震の避難訓練を行いました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Ren's town held an earthquake drill. Ren and his family left their house to join it. At the park, a firefighter taught the residents how to use a fire extinguisher, and Ren tried it himself. When they got home, Ren and his family packed water and food into an emergency bag. A few months later, however, Ren opened the bag and was surprised to find that the food had already passed its expiration date.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：町内放送が流れ、レンと家族が避難訓練に参加するために家を出ている。／2コマめ：公園で消防士が、消火器の使い方を住民に教えていて、レンが試している。／3コマめ：家に帰って、レンが家族と一緒に非常用バッグに水や食べ物を入れている。／4コマめ：数か月後、レンが非常用バッグを開けると、中の食べ物の賞味期限が切れていて、驚いている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Ren, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがレンだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that we should check our emergency bag regularly and replace old food so that we are always ready for a disaster.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think people in Japan are well prepared for natural disasters?
steps.ja: 日本の人々は自然災害への備えが十分にできていると思いますか。
steps.model: I think many people are prepared, but not enough. Schools hold drills regularly, so children know what to do. However, many families do not keep enough water or food at home, so they may have problems after a big disaster.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should every family be required to take part in a disaster drill?
steps.ja: すべての家庭に防災訓練への参加を義務づけるべきですか。
steps.model: I don't think it should be required, but it should be strongly encouraged. Some people are too busy or are not healthy enough to join. Instead, local governments could offer online drills or short sessions on weekends.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Kaito's class went to the city library." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、カイトのクラスは市の図書館へ行きました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Kaito's class went to the city library. A librarian introduced some books to the children, but Kaito looked bored. Then he happened to pick up a book about space, and he became so interested that he could not stop reading. That weekend, he went to a science museum with his father and watched a planetarium show. One night, however, Kaito read books for so long that he did not finish his homework. His mother was standing behind him with her arms crossed.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：図書館の司書が子どもたちに本を紹介していて、カイトは退屈そうにしている。／2コマめ：カイトがたまたま宇宙の本を手に取り、夢中になって読んでいる。／3コマめ：週末、カイトが父親と一緒に科学館でプラネタリウムを見ている。／4コマめ：夜、カイトが本を読みすぎて、机の上に宿題が終わらないまま残っていて、母親が腕を組んで見ている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Kaito's mother, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがカイトの母親だったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that I am happy he loves reading, but he must finish his homework before he reads for fun.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think young people today read fewer books than people in the past?
steps.ja: 今の若者は昔の人より本を読まなくなったと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Today, young people spend a lot of time on smartphones, video games, and online videos. However, many of them read on the Internet, so they may still be reading a lot in a different way.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should public libraries spend more money on digital services such as e-books?
steps.ja: 公共図書館は電子書籍などのデジタルサービスにもっとお金を使うべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think they should. E-books can be borrowed anytime from home, so people who are busy or live far from a library can use them. However, libraries should also keep paper books for people who prefer them.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Miyu went shopping with her mother at the supermarket." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、ミユは母親とスーパーへ買い物に行きました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Miyu went shopping with her mother at the supermarket. At the checkout, the clerk said that plastic bags were not free, and her mother realized that she had forgotten her shopping bag. When they got home, Miyu made a shopping bag from an old T-shirt. Later, she gave the bags she had made to her friends as presents, and they were very happy. A few weeks later, however, Miyu's room was full of bags and pieces of cloth, and her mother looked amazed.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：レジで店員が「レジ袋は有料です」と言い、母親がエコバッグを忘れたことに気づいている。／2コマめ：家でミユが古いTシャツを使ってエコバッグを作っている。／3コマめ：ミユが作ったエコバッグを友達にプレゼントしていて、友達が喜んでいる。／4コマめ：数週間後、ミユの部屋がエコバッグや布でいっぱいになっていて、母親があきれた顔をしている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Miyu's mother, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがミユの母親だったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that it is great that Miyu is creative, but she needs to clean up her room and not make too many bags.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think charging for plastic bags is an effective way to protect the environment?
steps.ja: レジ袋の有料化は環境を守るための効果的な方法だと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think it is effective. Since stores started charging for bags, many people bring their own bags. However, plastic bags are only a small part of plastic waste, so we also need to reduce other plastic packaging.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should people be encouraged to reuse old things instead of buying new ones?
steps.ja: 新しい物を買う代わりに古い物を再利用するよう、人々に勧めるべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Reusing old things reduces waste and saves money. For example, old clothes can be turned into bags or cleaning cloths, and used furniture can be sold to people who need it.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Daiki noticed many foreign tourists in his town." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、ダイキは町にたくさんの外国人観光客がいることに気づきました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Daiki noticed many foreign tourists in his town. Near the station, some tourists were holding a map and looked confused. Daiki bravely spoke to them in English and told them how to get to the old castle. After that, he and his friends made an English sightseeing map of their town. On the weekend, however, the area in front of the castle was so crowded with tourists that an old woman from the neighborhood could not get through.
steps.hint: 与えられた文で始めて、4コマを順番に過去形で説明しよう。However などでつなごう。
steps.scene: 1コマめ：駅前で外国人観光客が地図を持って困っていて、ダイキが見ている。／2コマめ：ダイキが勇気を出して英語で話しかけ、古いお城への行き方を教えている。／3コマめ：ダイキが友達と一緒に、町の英語の観光マップを作っている。／4コマめ：週末、お城の前が観光客でとても混雑していて、近所のおばあさんが通れずに困っているのをダイキが見ている。

steps.q: Please look at the fourth picture. If you were Daiki, what would you be thinking?
steps.ja: 4枚目の絵を見てください。もしあなたがダイキだったら、何を考えているでしょうか。
steps.model: I'd be thinking that tourists are good for our town, but we need to find a way to make sure local people can also live comfortably.
steps.hint: I'd be thinking that ... と始めて、気持ちとその理由を言おう。

steps.q: Do you think tourism is good for local communities?
steps.ja: 観光は地域社会にとってよいことだと思いますか。
steps.model: Yes, I think it is mostly good. Tourists spend money at local shops, hotels, and restaurants, so it creates jobs. However, if there are too many tourists, it can cause noise and traffic problems for residents.
steps.hint: Yes / No をはっきり言ってから、because や for example で理由を2つ言おう。

steps.q: Should Japanese students have more chances to communicate with people from other countries?
steps.ja: 日本の生徒は外国の人々と交流する機会をもっと持つべきですか。
steps.model: Yes, I think so. Talking with people from other countries helps students improve their English and understand different cultures. For example, schools could invite exchange students or hold online meetings with schools abroad.
steps.hint: I think ... で立場を示し、理由と具体例を続けよう。

steps.q: You have one minute to prepare. This is a story about a situation. Your story should begin with the following sentence: "One day, Shun's basketball team got a new coach." Please begin your narration. You have two minutes.
steps.ja: 1分間で準備してください。これはある状況についての物語です。物語は次の文で始めてください：「ある日、シュンのバスケットボールチームに新しいコーチが来ました。」 ナレーションを始めてください。時間は2分間です。
steps.model: One day, Shun's basketball team got a new coach. When the coach greeted the team in the gym, the players looked nervous.
